text: Which role should an application's managed identity receive to read secret values from a Key Vault that uses Azure RBAC?
explanation: Key Vault Secrets User reads secret contents. Contributor manages the vault resource and does not grant data access, and Crypto Officer is for keys.

text: In the Python SDK, what does SecretClient.get_secret('db-password') return?

options.text: The latest version of the secret

explanation: Without a version, get_secret returns the latest version. Pass a version as the second argument to read a specific one.

text: You call set_secret on an existing secret name with a new value. What happens?

options.text: A new version is created and older versions remain
An error because the secret exists

explanation: Secrets are versioned. Each set creates a new version, and a reference without a version resolves to the latest.

text: A database password must be rotated before it expires, using Azure services only for orchestration. Which design is typical?

options.text: Key Vault rotates every secret automatically with no setup
A timer trigger that deletes the secret
An Event Grid SecretNearExpiry event triggers a Function that creates the new credential and stores a new secret version

explanation: Key Vault emits SecretNearExpiry events through Event Grid. A Function subscribed to it rotates the credential and writes a new secret version. Automatic rotation policies exist for keys, not arbitrary secrets.

text: What is the minimum key rotation interval allowed in a Key Vault key rotation policy?

options.text: 7 days from creation and from expiry

explanation: The minimum value is seven days from creation and seven days from the expiration time.

text: An App Service setting uses a Key Vault reference with no version. A new secret version is created. What happens?

options.text: The app picks up the latest version automatically after a rotation
Nothing until you edit the setting

explanation: A versionless reference follows the latest version. A reference that pins a version never changes.

text: What does purge protection on a Key Vault do?

options.text: Prevents anyone from permanently purging a deleted vault or object until the retention period ends

explanation: Soft delete keeps deleted items recoverable for the retention period (7 to 90 days, default 90). Purge protection stops early permanent deletion.

text: The same App Configuration key, Shop:DbEndpoint, needs different values for Test, Staging and Production. What do you use?
explanation: A label distinguishes key-values that share a key. A key and a label identify one key-value, and no label is the null label.

text: An application needs a database password through App Configuration. What is the correct approach?

options.text: Store the password as a normal key-value
Store a Key Vault reference key-value; the app resolves it from Key Vault with its identity

explanation: App Configuration is not for secrets. A Key Vault reference stores only the secret URI, and the provider reads the secret from Key Vault.

text: You change ten related settings and want the application to reload them together, not one by one. Which App Configuration pattern helps?

options.text: A sentinel key watched with refresh_on, updated last

explanation: With a sentinel key, the app refreshes the whole selected set only when the sentinel changes, so you update it after the other settings.

text: Which role lets someone manage the key rotation policy of keys in a Key Vault using Azure RBAC?
explanation: Key Vault Crypto Officer manages keys, including the rotation policy and on-demand rotation.

text: What is the combined size limit of an Azure App Configuration key-value, including key, value and attributes?
explanation: There is a combined size limit of 10 KB on a key-value.

text: Which HTTP header carries the W3C trace context across services?
explanation: The W3C Trace Context standard uses the traceparent header with the trace id, parent span id and flags.

text: Where should the Application Insights connection string be set for a production workload using the OpenTelemetry distro?
explanation: The environment variable is recommended for production. Setting the connection string in code is for local development and test.

text: Three microservices send telemetry to one Application Insights resource and show up as a single node on the Application Map. What fixes it?

options.text: Set a distinct cloud role name for each service (the OpenTelemetry service.name)

explanation: With multiple services in one resource you must set cloud role names so the map and queries can tell them apart.

text: Which KQL query counts requests in 10 minute buckets over the last hour?

options.text: requests | where timestamp > ago(1h) | summarize count() by bin(timestamp, 10m)

explanation: summarize with bin(timestamp, 10m) aggregates per time bucket, and ago(1h) restricts the time range.

text: Which KQL query finds the targets of failing outgoing calls?

options.text: dependencies | where success == false | summarize count() by target

explanation: The dependencies table holds outgoing calls such as HTTP, database and Service Bus calls, with a success column and a target.

text: How can you correlate a request with the database call and the exception it caused?

options.text: Match the timestamp to the second
Match the operation_Id, which equals the trace id

explanation: All telemetry of one transaction shares the operation_Id (the trace id), so you can filter or join on it.

text: In a custom span you caught an exception and want the trace to show the failure. Which calls do you make on the span?
explanation: record_exception attaches the exception to the span and set_status marks the span as an error.

text: Which KQL operator returns the 10 slowest operations ordered by a computed percentile column named p95?
explanation: top n by column sorts and returns the first n rows. take n returns any n rows with no ordering.
